raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-SLE-ConnectivityAgMarketInfra",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Institutional fragmentation and weak coordination among multiple transport ministries and agencies may cause implementation delays and inefficiencies.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish clear inter‑agency coordination mechanisms, regular joint NPSC meetings, define roles and responsibilities, and use a centralized project coordination unit.",
      "evidence": "Key challenges ... institutional fragmentation, insufficient funding, and capacity constraints. Multiple agencies operating with overlapping responsibilities (Sectoral Context, paragraph 15)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Insufficient long‑term financing for operation and maintenance of bridges, roads and market facilities after project closure could erode benefits.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Create sustainable financing mechanisms (road fund, market user fees), embed O&M budgets in annual work plans, and train local councils on revenue collection.",
      "evidence": "Critical Assumptions state funding is available for maintenance; RMFA collected only US$12.5 M, a small fraction of needed support (Sectoral Context, paragraph 15)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Climate‑induced flooding and landslides may damage newly built bridges and roads, reducing service life.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Apply climate‑resilient design standards: oversized drainage, scour protection, flood‑proof deck heights, and conduct detailed hydrological modelling before construction.",
      "evidence": "Climate change expected to exacerbate flooding, landslides ... risks to bridges, roads and markets (Country Context, paragraph 10) and designs will follow climate‑proofed parameters (Component 2 description)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Procurement capacity gaps in the PCIU (no procurement unit, limited staff knowledge) risk delays, non‑compliance and fraud.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit qualified procurement specialist before effectiveness, conduct regular procurement clinics, use STEP for tracking, and strengthen bid evaluation committees.",
      "evidence": "PCIU does not have a procurement unit currently and it will be established and staffed... (Procurement section) and procurement risk assessment lists PCIU as not established (Annex 6)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Weak financial management capacity; FM risk rated high due to limited experience with World Bank procedures.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Centralize FM unit, hire FM specialist, provide targeted FM training, implement FM manual, and conduct periodic internal audits.",
      "evidence": "FM risk before mitigation is “High” mainly due to insufficient experience ... overall weak control environment (Annex 7)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Delay in establishing the National Project Steering Committee within 60 days may weaken oversight and coordination.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set a monitoring checklist, assign responsibility to MTA to convene NPSC within 30 days, and report status to the World Bank.",
      "evidence": "Legal covenant: Recipient shall establish a National Project Steering Committee no later than sixty (60) days of the Effective Date (Legal section)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Gender‑based violence and sexual harassment on public transport could undermine safety objectives and deter female users.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Install CCTV on buses, create a SH hotline, run awareness campaigns, and train operators on response protocols.",
      "evidence": "Component 1 sub‑component c mentions CCTV to reduce harassment; gender section outlines SH action plan (Gender aspects)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Low mobile‑phone penetration among rural women may limit uptake of the AMIS mobile app, reducing market information benefits.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide alternative channels (radio, community meetings), partner with women’s NGOs for outreach, and deliver training on app use.",
      "evidence": "Rural women have limited phone access; internet penetration 21.2 % (Component 3 description, paragraph on mobile access)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "High road‑safety risk; Sierra Leone’s poor safety record may lead to accidents during construction and operation.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement road‑safety training, improve signage, enforce speed limits, integrate safety audits into RAMS, and monitor incidents via the road‑safety database.",
      "evidence": "Sierra Leone has 33 road crash fatalities per 100 000 population, third highest in West Africa (Transport Connectivity, paragraph 8)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Activation of the Contingent Emergency Response Component may be delayed by procedural bottlenecks, limiting rapid disaster response.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Finalize CERC manual before implementation, conduct simulation exercises, pre‑approve trigger criteria, and keep standby funds readily accessible.",
      "evidence": "Component 5 description of CERC includes a manual and emergency action plan (Component 5)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Cost overruns common in the region; climate‑resilient designs may increase capital costs beyond budget.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Include a contingency reserve, apply value‑engineering, monitor expenditures via STEP, and adjust scope if necessary.",
      "evidence": "Sensitivity analysis assumes a 25 % increase in capital costs; 43 % of projects in Sub‑Saharan Africa experience >15 % overruns (Economic Analysis, paragraph 9)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Extreme weather during the rainy season could halt construction activities, causing schedule delays.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Schedule critical works in the dry season, use modular construction methods, and build weather‑contingency buffers into the timeline.",
      "evidence": "Construction will use incremental launching to avoid delays from prolonged rainy seasons (Component 2 description) and wet season regularly disrupts connectivity (Country Context, paragraph 2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Private‑sector lease‑operate‑own bus scheme risk of operator default or inability to meet lease payments.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct rigorous credit assessments, require performance bonds, monitor lease payments regularly, and include step‑in rights for the government.",
      "evidence": "Component 1 sub‑component c describes lease‑operate‑own scheme and private capital enabling (Private Capital Facilitation section)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Market infrastructure may be under‑utilized if not aligned with farmer needs, reducing expected economic returns.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Carry out participatory needs assessments, involve farmer groups in design, monitor usage, and adjust facilities based on feedback.",
      "evidence": "Needs assessment will adopt participatory processes, collect gender‑disaggregated data, and prioritize women’s perspectives (Gender aspects, Component 3)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Governance and corruption risk in procurement and contract award could lead to fraud and loss of value for money.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Enforce transparent bidding, publish award notices, use independent audits, implement anti‑corruption training, and monitor via STEP and CRPD.",
      "evidence": "Procurement risk assessment lists fraud, collusion, weak complaint redress; anti‑corruption guidelines apply (Annex 6 and Annex 7)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Limited capacity of SLRA to operate the Bridge Management System may delay asset‑management benefits.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Provide BMS training, develop user manuals, allocate dedicated staff, and pilot the system before full roll‑out.",
      "evidence": "Component 2 sub‑component c supports development of a digital bridge management system (BMS) and technical assistance includes software and user guidelines (Component 2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Inaccurate or delayed data feeding into AMIS could mislead farmers, reducing the platform’s effectiveness.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish data‑quality protocols, conduct regular verification, train data collectors, and maintain a manual backup reporting system.",
      "evidence": "Limited capacity to integrate wide variations of value chains and inadequate resources for timely data collection (Component 3 description)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Delay in recruitment of key project staff (procurement specialist, FM specialist, social specialist) could postpone procurement and financial processes.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Start recruitment early, use competitive selection, appoint interim staff if needed, and set firm recruitment timelines with performance incentives.",
      "evidence": "PCIU will recruit a procurement specialist, FM specialist, internal auditor and social specialist before project effectiveness (Implementation Arrangements)."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Institutional fragmentation and weak coordination among multiple transport ministries and agencies may cause implementation delays and inefficiencies.
risks.mitigation: Establish clear inter‑agency coordination mechanisms, regular joint NPSC meetings, define roles and responsibilities, and use a centralized project coordination unit.
risks.evidence: Key challenges ... institutional fragmentation, insufficient funding, and capacity constraints. Multiple agencies operating with overlapping responsibilities (Sectoral Context, paragraph 15).

risks.description: Insufficient long‑term financing for operation and maintenance of bridges, roads and market facilities after project closure could erode benefits.
risks.mitigation: Create sustainable financing mechanisms (road fund, market user fees), embed O&M budgets in annual work plans, and train local councils on revenue collection.
risks.evidence: Critical Assumptions state funding is available for maintenance; RMFA collected only US$12.5 M, a small fraction of needed support (Sectoral Context, paragraph 15).

risks.description: Climate‑induced flooding and landslides may damage newly built bridges and roads, reducing service life.
risks.mitigation: Apply climate‑resilient design standards: oversized drainage, scour protection, flood‑proof deck heights, and conduct detailed hydrological modelling before construction.
risks.evidence: Climate change expected to exacerbate flooding, landslides ... risks to bridges, roads and markets (Country Context, paragraph 10) and designs will follow climate‑proofed parameters (Component 2 description).

risks.description: Procurement capacity gaps in the PCIU (no procurement unit, limited staff knowledge) risk delays, non‑compliance and fraud.
risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified procurement specialist before effectiveness, conduct regular procurement clinics, use STEP for tracking, and strengthen bid evaluation committees.
risks.evidence: PCIU does not have a procurement unit currently and it will be established and staffed... (Procurement section) and procurement risk assessment lists PCIU as not established (Annex 6).

risks.description: Weak financial management capacity; FM risk rated high due to limited experience with World Bank procedures.
risks.mitigation: Centralize FM unit, hire FM specialist, provide targeted FM training, implement FM manual, and conduct periodic internal audits.
risks.evidence: FM risk before mitigation is “High” mainly due to insufficient experience ... overall weak control environment (Annex 7).

risks.description: Delay in establishing the National Project Steering Committee within 60 days may weaken oversight and coordination.
risks.mitigation: Set a monitoring checklist, assign responsibility to MTA to convene NPSC within 30 days, and report status to the World Bank.
risks.evidence: Legal covenant: Recipient shall establish a National Project Steering Committee no later than sixty (60) days of the Effective Date (Legal section).

risks.description: Gender‑based violence and sexual harassment on public transport could undermine safety objectives and deter female users.
risks.mitigation: Install CCTV on buses, create a SH hotline, run awareness campaigns, and train operators on response protocols.
risks.evidence: Component 1 sub‑component c mentions CCTV to reduce harassment; gender section outlines SH action plan (Gender aspects).

risks.description: Low mobile‑phone penetration among rural women may limit uptake of the AMIS mobile app, reducing market information benefits.
risks.mitigation: Provide alternative channels (radio, community meetings), partner with women’s NGOs for outreach, and deliver training on app use.
risks.evidence: Rural women have limited phone access; internet penetration 21.2 % (Component 3 description, paragraph on mobile access).

risks.description: High road‑safety risk; Sierra Leone’s poor safety record may lead to accidents during construction and operation.
risks.mitigation: Implement road‑safety training, improve signage, enforce speed limits, integrate safety audits into RAMS, and monitor incidents via the road‑safety database.
risks.evidence: Sierra Leone has 33 road crash fatalities per 100 000 population, third highest in West Africa (Transport Connectivity, paragraph 8).

risks.description: Activation of the Contingent Emergency Response Component may be delayed by procedural bottlenecks, limiting rapid disaster response.
risks.mitigation: Finalize CERC manual before implementation, conduct simulation exercises, pre‑approve trigger criteria, and keep standby funds readily accessible.
risks.evidence: Component 5 description of CERC includes a manual and emergency action plan (Component 5).

risks.description: Cost overruns common in the region; climate‑resilient designs may increase capital costs beyond budget.
risks.mitigation: Include a contingency reserve, apply value‑engineering, monitor expenditures via STEP, and adjust scope if necessary.
risks.evidence: Sensitivity analysis assumes a 25 % increase in capital costs; 43 % of projects in Sub‑Saharan Africa experience >15 % overruns (Economic Analysis, paragraph 9).

risks.description: Extreme weather during the rainy season could halt construction activities, causing schedule delays.
risks.mitigation: Schedule critical works in the dry season, use modular construction methods, and build weather‑contingency buffers into the timeline.
risks.evidence: Construction will use incremental launching to avoid delays from prolonged rainy seasons (Component 2 description) and wet season regularly disrupts connectivity (Country Context, paragraph 2).

risks.description: Private‑sector lease‑operate‑own bus scheme risk of operator default or inability to meet lease payments.
risks.mitigation: Conduct rigorous credit assessments, require performance bonds, monitor lease payments regularly, and include step‑in rights for the government.
risks.evidence: Component 1 sub‑component c describes lease‑operate‑own scheme and private capital enabling (Private Capital Facilitation section).

risks.description: Market infrastructure may be under‑utilized if not aligned with farmer needs, reducing expected economic returns.
risks.mitigation: Carry out participatory needs assessments, involve farmer groups in design, monitor usage, and adjust facilities based on feedback.
risks.evidence: Needs assessment will adopt participatory processes, collect gender‑disaggregated data, and prioritize women’s perspectives (Gender aspects, Component 3).

risks.description: Governance and corruption risk in procurement and contract award could lead to fraud and loss of value for money.
risks.mitigation: Enforce transparent bidding, publish award notices, use independent audits, implement anti‑corruption training, and monitor via STEP and CRPD.
risks.evidence: Procurement risk assessment lists fraud, collusion, weak complaint redress; anti‑corruption guidelines apply (Annex 6 and Annex 7).

risks.description: Limited capacity of SLRA to operate the Bridge Management System may delay asset‑management benefits.
risks.mitigation: Provide BMS training, develop user manuals, allocate dedicated staff, and pilot the system before full roll‑out.
risks.evidence: Component 2 sub‑component c supports development of a digital bridge management system (BMS) and technical assistance includes software and user guidelines (Component 2).

risks.description: Inaccurate or delayed data feeding into AMIS could mislead farmers, reducing the platform’s effectiveness.
risks.mitigation: Establish data‑quality protocols, conduct regular verification, train data collectors, and maintain a manual backup reporting system.
risks.evidence: Limited capacity to integrate wide variations of value chains and inadequate resources for timely data collection (Component 3 description).

risks.description: Delay in recruitment of key project staff (procurement specialist, FM specialist, social specialist) could postpone procurement and financial processes.
risks.mitigation: Start recruitment early, use competitive selection, appoint interim staff if needed, and set firm recruitment timelines with performance incentives.
risks.evidence: PCIU will recruit a procurement specialist, FM specialist, internal auditor and social specialist before project effectiveness (Implementation Arrangements).
